# client.availability()

AllocationService is the read-only half of the engine: it answers how much is
free, and never changes anything. HoldService is the half that takes.

The counting is done here rather than stored anywhere. No RFC models an
inventory count -- RFC 5545 and RFC 7953 are one-calendar-one-timeline -- so
"5 of 12 free" is produced by asking each RFC 9073 resource's calendar
whether it is free across the window and totalling the answers. RFC 7953's
VAVAILABILITY says when a resource was on offer at all; bookings on its
calendar say what has since been taken; the difference is availability.

Every operation is a custom method (AIP-136): they compute rather than fetch,
so they take neither the standard-method names nor their shapes.

`client.availability()` calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.AllocationService`. Every method is async and returns
`shokki_freebusy::Result`.

`async fn compute_availability(&self, request: ComputeAvailabilityRequest) -> Result<ComputeAvailabilityResponse>`

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.AllocationService.ComputeAvailability` (`POST /v1/resources:computeAvailability`).

Required: `window`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

```rust
use shokki_freebusy::{ComputeAvailabilityRequest, Freebusy, google_cloud_type};

async fn availability_compute_availability(client: &Freebusy) -> shokki_freebusy::Result<()> {
    let request =
        ComputeAvailabilityRequest::new().set_window(google_cloud_type::model::Interval::default());
    let result = client.availability().compute_availability(request).await?;
    println!("{result:?}");

}
```

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.AllocationService.CheckAvailability` (`POST /v1/resources:checkAvailability`).

Checks one exact window for one exact quantity, with reasons when it fails.

## client.availability().batch_compute_availability

`async fn batch_compute_availability(&self, request: BatchComputeAvailabilityRequest) -> Result<BatchComputeAvailabilityResponse>`

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.AllocationService.BatchComputeAvailability` (`POST /v1/resources:batchCompute`).

Runs several availability computations in one round trip.

Each entry is independent and may name different resources, a different
window or granularity. Capped at 50 entries, because each one fans out across every
candidate resource's calendar.

Required: `requests`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.AllocationService.SearchAvailability` (`POST /v1/resources:searchAvailability`).

Searches every resource for those free across a window.

The search entry point, where ComputeAvailability counts over resources
the caller has already chosen. Paginated, since a search may match
thousands of resources.

Required: `window`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

```rust

async fn availability_search_availability(client: &Freebusy) -> shokki_freebusy::Result<()> {
    let request =
        SearchAvailabilityRequest::new().set_window(google_cloud_type::model::Interval::default());
    let mut items = client
        .availability()
        .search_availability_auto_paging(request);
    while let Some(item) = items.next().await {
```
